A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VideoRoPE and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–8, Figures 1–9, and Appendices A–F. Textual and visual inspection supports comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original VideoRoPE evaluations, baseline comparisons, component ablations, and context-length extrapolation results.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results in Section 5 and Appendix A, including benchmark comparisons and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 4 corrects the specified ATS position assignment for text following video in Equation (7). LTA, spatial interleaving, and diagonal layout remain unchanged. This is a localized indexing-rule correction; the PDFs do not establish that the experimental implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both use the same LLaVA-Video-178k training subset and evaluate LongVideoBench, MLVU, Video-MME, V-NIAH, V-NIAH-D, and VideoHallucer. Appendix scenarios and needle examples are retained.

E2.justification: Vanilla RoPE, TAD-RoPE, and M-RoPE remain the evaluated comparators in the corresponding benchmark and extrapolation experiments. Citation-year suffix changes do not introduce different methods.

E3.justification: The reported training and evaluation settings are unchanged, including 8192-token training, frame sampling, 8k–64k evaluations, and Appendix A’s 128k experiment. Appendix B retains the same benchmark filtering, retrieval sampling, and distractor insertion procedures.

E4.justification: Both retain the module ablation, ATS scaling-factor sweep, sequential-versus-interleaved spatial allocation comparison, and 128k extrapolation analysis. Figures 3 and 9 provide the same attention case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for its experiments. The reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: Reported values and qualitative results are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 3 retains VideoRoPE’s 91.11/87.11 retrieval accuracies and M-RoPE’s 78.67/74.67; Table 8 retains VideoRoPE’s 55.64 at 128k.

T1.justification: Equation (7) replaces each ending-text coordinate T_s + δT_v + τ with τ + (δ − 1)T_v under the same global-index interval. This non-equivalent correction removes an extra T_s + T_v offset. The remaining mathematical definitions and frequency analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same four design criteria, three VideoRoPE components, V-NIAH-D contribution, and claimed advantages across retrieval, understanding, and hallucination tasks.

C2.justification: The explanations linking frequency allocation to local versus long-range attention and distractor susceptibility remain substantively unchanged. Appendix interpretations of scaling and interleaving are retained, with no new applicability boundaries or limitations.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including model initialization, training-data selection, hyperparameters, 704 A100 GPU hours, and vLLM inference. Both retain the same statement promising future code availability.

R1.justification: Appendix C adds citations to OmniAlign-V and MM-IFEngine within the existing vision-language-model discussion. Other reference changes update bibliographic metadata or publication status for retained works, without materially changing research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording edits in the introduction and attention analysis, adds a Chinese University of Hong Kong affiliation and correspondence information, and updates bibliography formatting. Section organization and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Expanded front matter and reference edits produce limited text and page-layout reflow. All figures and tables retain their content, organization, and numbering; no display is added or removed.

improvement.justification: The decisive improvement is Equation (7)’s correction: it removes an unintended position offset after video and aligns the formula with the continuous diagonal layout already described and illustrated. This improves mathematical correctness and faithful implementation. The added citations provide a small contextual benefit, while experimental evidence and conclusions remain unchanged.
